If sentiment is consistently positive in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative in the last 3–5 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

In mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment shifts from positive to negative, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to reflect sentiment reversal.

In late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains neutral or mixed, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to align with historical mean reversion.

If sentiment spikes to 1.0+ in last 3 days, apply a 1.0–2.0% upward adjustment to forecast only if price is below 70.00; otherwise, cap at 70.00.

If sentiment is 0.0–0.33 in last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to forecast if price is above 72.00; otherwise, no adjustment.
